sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: FactoryBot and Capybara are the two most used test support libraries in Rails, and the interview questions are practical rather than conceptual. For FactoryBot the depth markers are: build_stubbed (instantiates a model without touching the database — use this for unit tests to keep them fast), traits for variation, sequences for uniqueness, and the lazy attribute block for dynamic values. For Capybara the depth markers are: the js: true metadata flag that switches to a real browser driver (Selenium/Cuprite), the database-cleaner strategy issue (transactions don't work with JS tests because Capybara runs in a separate thread), and fill_in/click_button/have_text. The database-cleaner section explains transaction vs truncation strategy and when to use each.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: factory-bot-patterns, capybara-system-tests, database-cleaner. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
